actions.target: Lower circular edge of the large outer sleeve wall on the tubular heat-break assembly, at the z=7.5 boundary of the radius 3.45 mm cylinder
actions.relational_constraint: Apply the chamfer to the lower edge of the cylinder and match its size to the chamfer present on the top of the part.
actions.unresolved_reference: The target component and cylindrical face are localized as SOLID 3, section R04, feature F014, and FACE 749. The exact CadQuery EDGE index for the lower circular boundary of FACE 749 and the exact B-rep face representing the existing top chamfer are not individually classified in model.json; identify them by topology and measure the existing top chamfer before applying the new feature.
steps: Isolate SOLID 3, the tubular heat-break assembly in section R04. Do not modify the adjacent blocks, threaded nozzle variants, or the axial guide bore F015.

Use the semantic orientation mapping, for which CAD +Z is top and CAD -Z is bottom with confidence 0.78. This confirms that the requested lower edge is the negative-Z boundary of the main exterior cylinder rather than its upper rim.
Identify feature F014, the heat-break shaft and outer sleeve. Select FACE 749, the radius 3.45 mm cylindrical outer wall coaxial with CAD Z and extending from z=7.5 to z=20.8.

From the boundary edges of FACE 749, select the complete circular edge at z=7.5, centered approximately at CAD x=0 and y=-40. This is the lower edge of the largest cylindrical sleeve. Do not select the upper circular boundary near z=20.8.

Locate the existing chamfer at the top end of the same sleeve, adjacent to the upper boundary of FACE 749 and the upper annular seating face FACE 746 at z=21. The chamfer surface is contained among the unclassified SOLID 3 transition faces.

Measure the existing top chamfer's axial setback and radial setback from the adjoining cylindrical and annular faces. Preserve its chamfer definition exactly, including whether it is an equal-distance 45-degree chamfer or a distance-and-angle chamfer.
Create a new edge-chamfer feature on the selected lower circular edge of FACE 749. Set its distance or distance-angle parameters equal to the measured parameters of the existing top chamfer.

Orient the material removal so the outside diameter decreases toward the lower, negative-Z side, producing a continuous lead-in from the smaller lower region into the radius 3.45 mm sleeve. Preserve the central axial bore FACE 743 and all other stepped exterior regions.

Regenerate the model and verify that the chamfer forms one continuous annular conical face around the full circumference, without splitting FACE 749 unexpectedly or intersecting the adjacent lower transition geometry.

Confirm that the unchanged cylindrical portion retains radius 3.45 mm and remains coaxial with the axial guide bore F015. Confirm also that the new lower chamfer matches the top chamfer in both axial and radial extent.
Inspect the result in +X, -X, and iso1 views to verify that the new lower lead-in is on the main sleeve of the heat break and facilitates insertion into a mating cylindrical bore.

If a direct edge chamfer cannot be applied reliably to the imported STEP topology, reconstruct only the local axisymmetric exterior profile on a plane containing the CAD-Z axis. Copy the existing top-chamfer profile dimensions to the lower sleeve corner, revolve the revised profile through 360 degrees, and preserve the existing radius 1 mm axial bore and all unaffected exterior steps.

intention: Allow easier insertion of the part during assembly.
